maturity.title: Current maturity
maturity.body: Moriarty Webs is a concept under review. Supplied records include one current-Rust invoice-partial Groth16 roundtrip (S07) and seven finite local compiled-C2-wrapper cases (S08: one acceptance and six mutation rejections), with a single-party test setup whose operator can forge proofs and caller-fabricated proof contexts. No on-chain transaction is recorded. Only a conditional lowering argument is adopted. V2 consumer descriptions on this page are Opus readings of unadopted, uncompiled source, not observed behavior or exact-source correspondence to those runs. General Web integration, genuine intent authorization, onchain settlement and all-family compatibility remain unestablished in this packet. Local VM cost is not ledger cost. Every interactive example on this page is an illustration.

cards.title: What a verifying proof shows
cards.body: Under an honest setup and Groth16 knowledge soundness, a verifying proof shows the prover knew a witness satisfying the compiled constraints for its two public inputs. Linking those inputs to statement bytes additionally rests on the in-circuit BLAKE2b gadget and on BLAKE2b collision resistance. It never authenticates those bytes. A proof over supplied values does not make them an authenticated ledger fact or a true outside observation. A concrete execution proof, a universal property certificate and an authenticated ledger claim are different assertions; the latter two are not established Strand kinds.
assumptions: The current class-0 test setup is forgeable by its operator, so no production security claim follows.
Whether the compiled constraints and verifying key match your source is OPEN (T3: compiled circuit/VK and BLAKE2b gadget correspondence).
Outside facts keep their named issuer, predicate, authentication path and freshness limits.

Reference-input reads are PROPOSED: the validator must read the datum itself and authenticate its origin. PREMISE: being unspent at application shows presence only, with no exclusivity or history. A validity interval neither dates nor authenticates a datum.

SEC06-P06 PROPOSED; still needs real-context stale-sequence and expired-attestation cases, changed-reference-datum and forged-origin negatives, N5/N7–N9 at V, and a separately scoped real-context proof.

cards.title: Setup and keys
cards.body: The current test setup can be forged by its operator; whether the verifying key matches the compiled relation is OPEN. Groth16 needs a separate setup per distinct compiled circuit (R1CS matrices), not per logical predicate. In the current Rust source the predicate digest is a circuit constant, so each distinct relation identity is a distinct circuit. The required total setup count is unknown; predicate, catalogue and family counts do not determine it. No production ceremony is recorded in the supplied sources, and none is proposed here.
assumptions: A future universal circuit or Midnight's universal PLONK/KZG SRS would change the comparison (PROPOSED or target-specific).

V2 SOURCE READING: catalogue VK digests are fixed at genesis and carried unchanged, and Close requires zero balances and duties, so any key change needs a PROPOSED key migration action that carries residual duties.
Intent revocation (Revoke) advances seq; it is not key migration.
SEC06-P07 PROPOSED; still needs an old-VK-refused-after-migration negative, a setup-class report and independent review of any future ceremony.
cards.evidenceStage: RECORDED limitation (forgeable test setup); V2 SOURCE READING; total setup count UNKNOWN

cards.title: What ties a Strand to its step
cards.body: V2 SOURCE READING: tag, family, predicate_digest, shape_digest and body_len are circuit constants; the context fields vk_digest through intents_digest (bytes 112..339, including claimant_vkh) are free booleanized witness bits that are hashed, not interpreted. The consumer, not the circuit, ties those fields to the transaction: the settling validator rebuilds each statement from the transaction and the spent thread state, so a claim made for another thread step, catalogue, claimant or intent set does not match. Claimant binding happens at consumption, not at issuance: C2 Issue does not compare the claimant with the statement, so a mismatched envelope can be minted but cannot settle. This source-level binding is separate from T3, which stays OPEN.
assumptions: The class-0 setup operator can forge a proof for any digest and any claimant. The claimant is prover-chosen bytes, not an authenticated prover identity.
Builders select claim inputs; the ledger spends each claim once (PREMISE). A copied proof can be re-issued with the same claimant and a new expiry; only that claimant can release it.

Catalogue program_hash and source_hash are visible, covered by catalogue_digest and signed in every owner intent. No on-chain check links them to predicate_digest or vk_digest: that link is a CATALOGUE-AUTHOR ASSERTION and VK-to-matrix is OPEN. Exact predicate-digest field coverage depends on identity.rs, which the reviewer did not read.
The statement's network byte is declared by the catalogue and not compared with the executing ledger; separation across networks rests on outref uniqueness (PREMISE).

SEC06-P03 and SEC06-P04 PROPOSED; still need competing-claimant and same-claimant duplicate negatives, second-party source→relation→predicate reproduction, refusal-list coverage, N5/N7–N9, a T3 method, reviewed T2/T3 and F07–F10, a non-test setup, and cross-network replay analysis if the network byte is relied on.
cards.evidenceStage: V2 SOURCE READING (unadopted, uncompiled); T3 OPEN

cards.title: Where proofs are checked: the issuance route
cards.body: In the reviewed V2 source, each proof is checked when its claim is issued: the C2 claim policy checks a Groth16 proof and mints one claim output per Issue transaction. Claims must exist before settlement. The settlement transaction consumes them, recomputes each statement and compares it with the digest checked at issuance; it does not verify the proof again. Each consumed claim needs its claimant's signature on the settlement transaction and the burn of its token. Structurally, n required Strands mean n Issue transactions plus one settlement, excluding one-time genesis and any post-expiry reclaim. These counts are readings of uncompiled source, not measurements.
assumptions: Each claim output locks min-ADA from issuance until settlement or claimant-signed reclaim after the claimant-chosen expiry. Several envelopes can exist per statement digest.

Safe but not live: any catalogue account may Revoke (advancing seq), and a competing settlement may spend the outref, orphaning issued claims and locking their value until expiry. Earlier reclaim is PROPOSED (OPEN).

Batch issuance needs a C2 change (PROPOSED). Proof-at-consumption is a different PROPOSED design needing a new redeemer and in-settlement pairings, with size and budget unmeasured. Mempool chaining is a node premise outside the sources.
V2 source already refuses two claims for one consumed outref; S09's role-level refusal is an unadopted proposal and not deduplication permission.
Owner intents are signed before proving; claimant settlement signatures are a later, distinct event. Proof collection or claim-output creation executes no effect.
Still needs orphan-after-Revoke, competing-settlement and post-expiry reclaim cases, and a qualified complete-path measurement of both verification placements.
cards.evidenceStage: V2 SOURCE READING (structural); not observed onchain

cards.title: Complete and incomplete Webs
cards.body: PROPOSED: a Web settles only when every Strand its contract requires is present. An incomplete Web has no authority over thread effects. On the issuance route its already-issued claim outputs exist on-chain, lock value, and remain releasable only by their claimant. In the first proposed supported profile, the consumer refuses universal property certificates, authenticated-history claims, private handoff, recursive parents and multiparent joins as UNSUPPORTED; they remain required Web tracks, each needing its own trust path and evidence before any profile accepts it.
assumptions: All-or-nothing acceptance and a consumer-derived required set are PROPOSED; no Web consumer, second genuine relation or general cardinality exists in this packet.

Depicting several Strand roles does not establish separate relations or producers. A whole-execution proof may cover several claim specifications; naming source expressions fee or liability does not create independent proof producers.

A01 adopts only conditional T1: the all-role conjunction equals whole-action Core over one decoded body, modulo premise G including output well-formedness, a covering WebPlan, whole-action compilation first and the same field. There is no implementation, no T2, no T3 and no full WP migration (F07–F10); builder reliance is not permitted.
OPEN: whether a consumer can enforce a fully authorized partial financial step that carries every proof that step requires, distinct from a missing proof.

SEC06-P01 and SEC06-P02 PROPOSED; still need N1/N12 and unknown-class refusal, a report-level test that an incomplete set never renders as accepted, N1–N4/N6/N11/N14 at H/V, a wrong-action-index case, a required-set display, separate future-profile designs and fresh security review of reused V2 mechanisms.

cards.title: Effects, allocation and authority
cards.body: V2 SOURCE READING: owner intents sign per-asset gross_cap, fee_cap, net_floor and liability_cap for a beneficiary, a validity window, nonce = seq and the target predicate, VK and shape digests. Duties change only through recorded accruals and discharges, and a thread with a nonzero duty cannot close. The thread datum carries the complete custody snapshot, which custody must equal exactly. Actual output allocation is the consuming validator's job; a proof can attest arithmetic only over values the validator recomputes. A profile chooses either strict one-output-per-obligation or a consumer-recomputed amount partition that admits coalesced payments, with every obligation allocated exactly once.
assumptions: The source strict-output rule covers redeemers of one S2 script hash only, not other scripts or S2 versions. No input value may count toward two obligations; ledger single-spend alone is not a value partition.
Circuit-level NotBound/TouchedOnly limits remain. A general multi-UTxO authenticated frame, role sets, cross-script allocation and partial-completion rules are PROPOSED.
No genuine intent signature is observed in the supplied proof records.

A supplied approved=true is consented to by the effect-derived required signers, and by a listed advancer if any; that is the debited account's consent, not a separate governance decision. A distinct approver must be a required signer, an advancer or an authenticated input.

SEC06-P05 PROPOSED; still needs double-satisfaction negatives across scripts and S2 versions, a coalesced positive under partition, fee-over-cap and dropped-duty cases, the approver-coverage lint, a genuine validator-checked signature in real context, and independent custody/duty/backing accounting with a backing-policy negative.
cards.evidenceStage: V2 SOURCE READING; allocation policy PROPOSED per profile

cards.title: Duties, backing and fees
cards.body: S12 and S13 source behavior requires non-negative custody, not full backing of liabilities. S12 funds escrow at 110: partial(35) debits 37 and leaves 73 against duties of 75 (invoice 65, reserve 10), which is 2 short. Funding 112 would back one partial; each further partial charges another 2 that no duty reflects. That backing is a PROPOSED application policy. S12 has no extra transfer and no reserve-duty-return action; after finish, escrow holds 8 against reserve duty 10, and the nonzero reserve duty blocks V2 Close. S13 allocate(true,23,7,2) needs at least 23 A and 4 B for non-negative custody; 25 A and 10 B is PROPOSED full backing, and S13 has no action discharging allocation_reserve.
assumptions: Source-only arithmetic, not execution. The V2 Close zero-duty condition is an uncompiled-source reading.
Even under the proposed 112 policy the reserve duty stays 10 and Close stays blocked; discharge or migration needs a program change.
S13 units is checked only arithmetically (23 = 3×7 + 2) and is never debited.

A program-asset fee is not debt repayment and not a network fee. Network fees, collateral, claim-output min-ADA and the V2 thread reserve (lovelace returned on Close) are separate funding items; a reserve duty is a program liability.
Delivery evidence and dispute rules remain named assumptions. Still needs independent open/partial/finish/reserve-return accounting and a backing-policy negative.

glossaryClarifications.clarification: An individual proof with its claim, statement and binding metadata. Before a proof exists, say requirement or planned proof. A signed owner intent, UTxO, claim output, validator, catalogue entry, pattern or predicate is not a Strand.

PROPOSED: the contract-fixed set of required Strands for one transition, accepted all-or-nothing by the consuming validator in a supported profile. Profiles refuse unsupported classes; certificates, authenticated history, private handoff, recursion and bounded multiparent remain required future tracks.
The reusable type of a Strand; not itself a proof. Reusing a specification does not reuse a proof for changed state.
V2 SOURCE READING: a C2 UTxO holding one token named H(envelope), minted after the claim policy's Groth16 check. It confers no authority by itself and is neither the proof nor its validator.
Issuance is the reviewed V2 route. Verification at consumption is PROPOSED and needs a new redeemer and in-settlement pairings.
Thread reserve is V2 lovelace returned on Close. A reserve duty is a program liability such as S12 reserve or S13 allocation_reserve.
Revoke advances seq to cancel outstanding intents and can orphan issued claims. Key migration (VK change) is PROPOSED; V2 catalogues are immutable.
A per-profile choice between strict one-output-per-obligation (reviewed V2 scope: one S2 script hash) and a consumer-recomputed amount partition.
thread is a V2 source identifier for the consumer's state instance (thread id, thread effects, thread reserve). It is not a public synonym for Strand; public vocabulary is Web and Strand.
ILLUSTRATION: every illustrated requirement has an illustrated Strand. It is not proof verification, acceptance or settlement.
Actual target-ledger acceptance of the authorized effects under the applicable conditions. Nothing on this page settles anything.
A link stated by the catalogue author and not checked on-chain, here between program_hash/source_hash and predicate_digest/vk_digest.
A Cardano ledger rule assumed by the reasoning but not contained in the sources, for example single spending of an outref.

main.heroBody: Moriarty Webs let a Cardano financial application bring the required proofs to a transition. The consuming contract names every Strand it needs — the payment arithmetic, the fee, the duties that continue — and its validator accepts the transition only when each one is present and matches a statement rebuilt from the transaction itself. Owners sign exact limits on what can leave their accounts, fees stay separate from repayment, and what is still owed stays on the record. Webs are built for Cardano developers writing financial dapps, and for the wallets, asset issuers and transaction builders that work alongside them.
main.explorerIntro: Choose one of five financial transitions. Each Web lists the Strands its contract requires and the exact statement each one proves. A role names a condition the transition must prove; one whole-execution proof can cover several roles. Remove a Strand to see how the consuming contract treats an incomplete Web.
main.proofRoleExplanation: Each Strand carries one proof, and a proof does one job: it shows that the Strand’s statement holds — that the payment, fee, limits and duty updates are computed correctly from the values the statement contains. A proof cannot show that those values describe the real ledger. Ledger facts — which state is being spent, which outputs exist, who signed — come from the transaction itself. That is why the settling validator rebuilds every statement from the transaction and the state it spends, and accepts a Strand only when the rebuilt statement matches the one whose proof was checked at issuance. Facts from outside the chain, such as a delivery document or a price, enter only with a named issuer, an authentication path and a freshness limit. The proof supplies correct computation; the validator supplies authenticated premises and scope.

definitions.body: The complete set of Strands a consuming contract requires for one transition. The contract fixes the set and the validator accepts it all-or-nothing: with every required Strand present and matching, the transition can settle; with any one missing, it has no authority over the contract’s effects. Each profile states which kinds of Strand it accepts and refuses the rest.

One proof together with its claim, its statement and the metadata that binds it to a single step: the state being spent, its sequence number, the settling script, the catalogue, the signed intents and the claimant. Signed intents, UTxOs, proof-claim outputs, validators and catalogue entries are not Strands.

The reusable type of a Strand: what is asserted, about which subject, under which premises and for which relation. Many Strands share one specification; reusing a specification never reuses a proof for changed state.

main.assemblyComplete: Complete Web. Every required Strand is present, so the transition can go to settlement, where the validator rebuilds each statement from the transaction and enforces the signed effects.
main.assemblyIncomplete: Incomplete Web. A required Strand is missing, so the transition has no authority over the contract’s effects. Proof-claim outputs already issued stay on-chain, hold their min-ADA, and only their claimant can release them.

main.lifecycleTitle: From signed intent to settled transition
main.lifecycleIntro: A transition moves through four stages. Signing, proving, issuing proof claims and settling are separate events, and no application effect happens until settlement.

lifecycleSteps.title: Authorize the outcome
lifecycleSteps.body: Each owner signs an intent before any proof exists. Per asset, it caps what can leave the account in total, in fees and as new liability, and sets the minimum net result for each beneficiary. It also names the validity window, a one-time nonce and the exact relation and verifying key the proofs must use.

lifecycleSteps.title: Produce the Strands
lifecycleSteps.body: A prover runs the program and produces a proof for each Strand the Web requires. Each statement names one step: the state being spent, its sequence number, the settling script, the catalogue, the signed intents and the claimant. One whole-execution proof can serve several roles.

lifecycleSteps.title: Issue proof claims
lifecycleSteps.body: Each proof goes on-chain in its own Issue transaction. The claim policy checks the Groth16 proof and mints one proof-claim output, which holds min-ADA until settlement consumes it or its claimant reclaims it after expiry. Proof-claim issuance records checked evidence. It never mints the application’s own asset and moves no application funds.

lifecycleSteps.title: Settle and read back
lifecycleSteps.body: One settlement transaction consumes every required proof-claim output. The validator rebuilds each statement from the transaction and the state it spends, compares it with the digest checked at issuance, requires each claimant’s signature, burns each claim token, and enforces the signed caps, payments and continuing duties. The application then confirms inclusion, waits for the finality it needs and reads back the actual outputs and remaining duties.

faqs.question: Does issuing a proof claim mint my token?
faqs.answer: No. Proof-claim issuance and application-asset minting are separate. Issuing a proof claim puts checked evidence on-chain as a proof-claim output; that token exists only to be consumed by a settlement, where it is burned. Your application asset is minted only by its own minting policy, which enforces the cap, the supply continuation and the recipients.

faqs.question: Do I need approval from Moriarty to build with Webs?
faqs.answer: No. Moriarty tooling is permissionless: any developer can write, compile, prove and deploy programs in the supported language without approval from Moriarty maintainers, a council, a campaign or a program registry. What still applies is objective: the ledger’s validity rules and resource costs, and the authorization of the owners whose assets move. A program can still set its own access rules for its own users.

faqs.question: What does an owner actually approve?
faqs.answer: An intent, signed before any proof is made. For each asset it caps the gross amount that can leave the account, the fees and any new liability, and it sets the minimum net amount each beneficiary must receive. It also names a validity window, a one-time nonce and the exact relation the proofs must satisfy. The signing view presents those limits in plain terms, together with the payment, the fee and the duties that remain afterward, with network fees shown separately.

faqs.question: Who signs what, and when?
faqs.answer: Owners sign their intents first, before proving. Each Issue transaction carries one proof; the claim policy checks it and mints one proof-claim output that names its claimant. The settlement transaction consumes those outputs, so it carries each claimant’s signature and burns each claim token, while the contract checks the signed intents of the accounts the effects debit. A claim that is never used comes back through a reclaim its claimant signs after the expiry they chose. Implementation and evidence records where the per-transaction signer list stands today.

faqs.question: How does an application know the transition happened?
faqs.answer: It observes three separate things: the transaction’s inclusion, the finality the application requires, and a full readback of the actual outputs and remaining duties. It then reconciles those per-asset effects against what each owner signed. A timeout means the outcome is unknown, not that nothing happened.

faqs.question: Is a remaining duty a missing proof?
faqs.answer: No. A partial payment is ordinary financial progress: the payment step carries every Strand it requires, and the unpaid invoice and reserve duties continue on the record. A missing Strand is different — it leaves the transition with no authority at all.

faqs.question: What happens to proof claims if a Web never settles?
faqs.answer: They stay on-chain and keep holding their min-ADA. Only the claimant can release them, either through settlement or through reclaim after the expiry the claimant chose. If the owners’ intents are revoked, or another settlement spends the same state first, those claims can no longer settle and wait for that expiry.

faqs.question: Do more Strands mean lower cost?
faqs.answer: Not by themselves. Each required Strand is issued in its own transaction before one settlement transaction consumes them all, and each proof-claim output holds min-ADA until it is consumed or reclaimed. A single whole-execution proof covering several roles is often the simpler design. Webs make every condition explicit and inspectable; cost comparisons come from measurement on the target network.

roles.statement: Two orders each offer 100 A and require at least 90 B net; each owner receives 92 B.
roles.authentication: Asset identities and each owner’s limits come from the owners’ signed intents; the validator checks the actual outputs.

roles.label: Pool arithmetic
roles.claim: The pool continuation follows the pool’s relation.
roles.statement: The reserve update, fee rule and exact rounding agree with both orders.
roles.authentication: Pool reserves come from the pool state being spent; any outside price carries its named source and freshness limit.

roles.label: Batch accounting
roles.claim: Order and pool amounts agree across the batch.
roles.statement: The amounts used for each owner’s result are the amounts in the batch accounting, and no payment counts toward two orders.
roles.authentication: The consuming validator allocates actual outputs under its profile’s rule: one output per order, or an exact partition that admits combined payments with every order allocated once.

roles.claim: The supply update stays within the cap.
roles.statement: First issue: 300 units under a cap of 1,000; unissued capacity is 700.
roles.authentication: The application asset’s own minting policy enforces the cap and continues the supply state from its predecessor.

roles.claim: The recipient allocation totals the issued amount.
roles.statement: Recipient one receives 180 units and recipient two receives 120 units; 180 + 120 = 300.
roles.authentication: The minting policy and the consuming validator check the actual mint and recipient outputs.

roles.label: Duty accounting
roles.claim: Servicing duties remain separate from token supply.
roles.statement: The remaining 700 units of capacity are not debt. A redemption promise is a duty only when the program defines it.
roles.authentication: A servicing duty names its parties, its exact asset and its creation and discharge rules; eligibility documents keep their issuer and freshness limits.

roles.statement: Debt 100 CASH plus accrual 5 CASH gives a duty of 105 CASH.

roles.label: Payment accounting

technical.summary: The page above describes Moriarty Webs as designed. This section records where the implementation stands. Supplied records include one current-Rust invoice-partial Groth16 roundtrip (S07) and seven local compiled-C2-wrapper cases (S08: one acceptance and six mutation rejections), with a single-party test setup whose operator can forge proofs and caller-fabricated proof contexts. No on-chain transaction is recorded. Descriptions of the consumer, claim policy, owner intents, duties and Close are Opus readings of unadopted, uncompiled V2 Aiken/Rust source, not observed behavior, and no supplied record pins the S07/S08 binaries or compiled bytes to that source. Of the composition argument, only conditional T1 is adopted; T2, T3 (compiled circuit/VK/BLAKE2b gadget correspondence) and the full WP migration are open. S08’s local VM figures are not ledger cost, and no cost, latency or portability advantage is measured or claimed.
technical.sourceVersusDesign: Invoice. The worksheet uses the fee-funded design: escrow opens with 112 CASH. The executed source differs. S12 open(90,10) funds escrow with exactly 110 CASH (invoice duty 100 = 90 + 10, reserve duty 10) and charges the buyer a separate 3 CASH opening fee, a gross debit of 113. On that source path one partial of amount a debits a + 2 and leaves 110 − a − 2 against duties of 110 − a: always 2 short (at 35: debit 37, cash 73 against duties 65 + 10 = 75). S12 checks only non-negative custody, not backing, and has no extra-funding transfer, so 112 needs a program change and a consumer-enforced backing policy. The buyer’s opening debit under the 112 design is not specified by any source. 112 backs one partial only; each further partial charges escrow another 2 that no duty reflects, so a sequence of partials needs a further funding rule. S12 has no reserve-duty-return action: after finish the source path leaves 8 against reserve duty 10 and the 112 path leaves 10 against 10, and the nonzero reserve duty blocks V2 Close on either path; discharge or migration needs a program change. Treasury. S13 allocate(true,23,7,2) needs only 23 A and 4 B for non-negative custody; holding 25 A and 10 B so that 2 A and 6 B remain is a full-backing policy a consumer must enforce. units is checked only arithmetically (23 = 3×7 + 2) and is never debited. rebate(amount) can discharge the B rebate; S13 has no action discharging allocation_reserve, so Close stays blocked. trustNotes.title: What a verifying proof shows
trustNotes.body: Under an honest setup and Groth16 knowledge soundness, a verifying proof shows the prover knew a witness satisfying the compiled constraints for its two public inputs. Linking those inputs to statement bytes additionally rests on the in-circuit BLAKE2b gadget and on BLAKE2b collision resistance. It never authenticates those bytes. A proof over supplied values does not make them an authenticated ledger fact or a true outside observation. A concrete execution proof, a universal property certificate and an authenticated ledger claim are different assertions; the latter two are not established Strand kinds.
assumptions: The current class-0 test setup is forgeable by its operator, so no production security claim follows.
Whether the compiled constraints and verifying key match your source is OPEN (T3: compiled circuit/VK and BLAKE2b gadget correspondence).
Outside facts keep their named issuer, predicate, authentication path and freshness limits.

Reference-input reads are PROPOSED: the validator must read the datum itself and authenticate its origin. PREMISE: being unspent at application shows presence only, with no exclusivity or history. A validity interval neither dates nor authenticates a datum.

SEC06-P06 PROPOSED; still needs real-context stale-sequence and expired-attestation cases, changed-reference-datum and forged-origin negatives, N5/N7–N9 at V, and a separately scoped real-context proof.

One genuine proof was accepted by a compiled C2 wrapper in a local VM with fabricated context (S08); no on-chain transaction is recorded. S08 /cases/0 records cpu 2222340191 and mem 205312 for the whole compiled C2 Issue evaluation, including its pairing; it is neither an isolated verification cost nor ledger ExUnits, fee or transaction fit. Every recorded proof context in the supplied sources is caller-fabricated (S07, S08).
assumptions: No supplied record pins the recorded runs to the later V2 source bytes; V2 readings elsewhere on this page are not evidence about these runs.
Named runtime guards behind the six S08 rejections were not instrumented.

trustNotes.title: Setup and keys
trustNotes.body: The current test setup can be forged by its operator; whether the verifying key matches the compiled relation is OPEN. Groth16 needs a separate setup per distinct compiled circuit (R1CS matrices), not per logical predicate. In the current Rust source the predicate digest is a circuit constant, so each distinct relation identity is a distinct circuit. The required total setup count is unknown; predicate, catalogue and family counts do not determine it. No production ceremony is recorded in the supplied sources, and none is proposed here.
assumptions: A future universal circuit or Midnight's universal PLONK/KZG SRS would change the comparison (PROPOSED or target-specific).

V2 SOURCE READING: catalogue VK digests are fixed at genesis and carried unchanged, and Close requires zero balances and duties, so any key change needs a PROPOSED key migration action that carries residual duties.
Intent revocation (Revoke) advances seq; it is not key migration.
SEC06-P07 PROPOSED; still needs an old-VK-refused-after-migration negative, a setup-class report and independent review of any future ceremony.
trustNotes.evidenceStage: RECORDED limitation (forgeable test setup); V2 SOURCE READING; total setup count UNKNOWN

trustNotes.title: What ties a Strand to its step
trustNotes.body: V2 SOURCE READING: tag, family, predicate_digest, shape_digest and body_len are circuit constants; the context fields vk_digest through intents_digest (bytes 112..339, including claimant_vkh) are free booleanized witness bits that are hashed, not interpreted. The consumer, not the circuit, ties those fields to the transaction: the settling validator rebuilds each statement from the transaction and the spent thread state, so a claim made for another thread step, catalogue, claimant or intent set does not match. Claimant binding happens at consumption, not at issuance: C2 Issue does not compare the claimant with the statement, so a mismatched envelope can be minted but cannot settle. This source-level binding is separate from T3, which stays OPEN.
assumptions: The class-0 setup operator can forge a proof for any digest and any claimant. The claimant is prover-chosen bytes, not an authenticated prover identity.
Builders select claim inputs; the ledger spends each claim once (PREMISE). A copied proof can be re-issued with the same claimant and a new expiry; only that claimant can release it.

Catalogue program_hash and source_hash are visible, covered by catalogue_digest and signed in every owner intent. No on-chain check links them to predicate_digest or vk_digest: that link is a CATALOGUE-AUTHOR ASSERTION and VK-to-matrix is OPEN. Exact predicate-digest field coverage depends on identity.rs, which the reviewer did not read.
The statement's network byte is declared by the catalogue and not compared with the executing ledger; separation across networks rests on outref uniqueness (PREMISE).

SEC06-P03 and SEC06-P04 PROPOSED; still need competing-claimant and same-claimant duplicate negatives, second-party source→relation→predicate reproduction, refusal-list coverage, N5/N7–N9, a T3 method, reviewed T2/T3 and F07–F10, a non-test setup, and cross-network replay analysis if the network byte is relied on.
trustNotes.evidenceStage: V2 SOURCE READING (unadopted, uncompiled); T3 OPEN

trustNotes.title: Where proofs are checked: the issuance route
trustNotes.body: In the reviewed V2 source, each proof is checked when its claim is issued: the C2 claim policy checks a Groth16 proof and mints one claim output per Issue transaction. Claims must exist before settlement. The settlement transaction consumes them, recomputes each statement and compares it with the digest checked at issuance; it does not verify the proof again. Each consumed claim needs its claimant's signature on the settlement transaction and the burn of its token. Structurally, n required Strands mean n Issue transactions plus one settlement, excluding one-time genesis and any post-expiry reclaim. These counts are readings of uncompiled source, not measurements.
assumptions: Each claim output locks min-ADA from issuance until settlement or claimant-signed reclaim after the claimant-chosen expiry. Several envelopes can exist per statement digest.

Safe but not live: any catalogue account may Revoke (advancing seq), and a competing settlement may spend the outref, orphaning issued claims and locking their value until expiry. Earlier reclaim is PROPOSED (OPEN).

Batch issuance needs a C2 change (PROPOSED). Proof-at-consumption is a different PROPOSED design needing a new redeemer and in-settlement pairings, with size and budget unmeasured. Mempool chaining is a node premise outside the sources.
V2 source already refuses two claims for one consumed outref; S09's role-level refusal is an unadopted proposal and not deduplication permission.
Owner intents are signed before proving; claimant settlement signatures are a later, distinct event. Proof collection or claim-output creation executes no effect.
Still needs orphan-after-Revoke, competing-settlement and post-expiry reclaim cases, and a qualified complete-path measurement of both verification placements.
trustNotes.evidenceStage: V2 SOURCE READING (structural); not observed onchain

trustNotes.title: Complete and incomplete Webs
trustNotes.body: PROPOSED: a Web settles only when every Strand its contract requires is present. An incomplete Web has no authority over thread effects. On the issuance route its already-issued claim outputs exist on-chain, lock value, and remain releasable only by their claimant. In the first proposed supported profile, the consumer refuses universal property certificates, authenticated-history claims, private handoff, recursive parents and multiparent joins as UNSUPPORTED; they remain required Web tracks, each needing its own trust path and evidence before any profile accepts it.
assumptions: All-or-nothing acceptance and a consumer-derived required set are PROPOSED; no Web consumer, second genuine relation or general cardinality exists in this packet.

Depicting several Strand roles does not establish separate relations or producers. A whole-execution proof may cover several claim specifications; naming source expressions fee or liability does not create independent proof producers.

A01 adopts only conditional T1: the all-role conjunction equals whole-action Core over one decoded body, modulo premise G including output well-formedness, a covering WebPlan, whole-action compilation first and the same field. There is no implementation, no T2, no T3 and no full WP migration (F07–F10); builder reliance is not permitted.
OPEN: whether a consumer can enforce a fully authorized partial financial step that carries every proof that step requires, distinct from a missing proof.

SEC06-P01 and SEC06-P02 PROPOSED; still need N1/N12 and unknown-class refusal, a report-level test that an incomplete set never renders as accepted, N1–N4/N6/N11/N14 at H/V, a wrong-action-index case, a required-set display, separate future-profile designs and fresh security review of reused V2 mechanisms.

trustNotes.title: Effects, allocation and authority
trustNotes.body: V2 SOURCE READING: owner intents sign per-asset gross_cap, fee_cap, net_floor and liability_cap for a beneficiary, a validity window, nonce = seq and the target predicate, VK and shape digests. Duties change only through recorded accruals and discharges, and a thread with a nonzero duty cannot close. The thread datum carries the complete custody snapshot, which custody must equal exactly. Actual output allocation is the consuming validator's job; a proof can attest arithmetic only over values the validator recomputes. A profile chooses either strict one-output-per-obligation or a consumer-recomputed amount partition that admits coalesced payments, with every obligation allocated exactly once.
assumptions: The source strict-output rule covers redeemers of one S2 script hash only, not other scripts or S2 versions. No input value may count toward two obligations; ledger single-spend alone is not a value partition.
Circuit-level NotBound/TouchedOnly limits remain. A general multi-UTxO authenticated frame, role sets, cross-script allocation and partial-completion rules are PROPOSED.
No genuine intent signature is observed in the supplied proof records.

A supplied approved=true is consented to by the effect-derived required signers, and by a listed advancer if any; that is the debited account's consent, not a separate governance decision. A distinct approver must be a required signer, an advancer or an authenticated input.

SEC06-P05 PROPOSED; still needs double-satisfaction negatives across scripts and S2 versions, a coalesced positive under partition, fee-over-cap and dropped-duty cases, the approver-coverage lint, a genuine validator-checked signature in real context, and independent custody/duty/backing accounting with a backing-policy negative.

trustNotes.title: Duties, backing and fees
trustNotes.body: S12 and S13 source behavior requires non-negative custody, not full backing of liabilities. S12 funds escrow at 110: partial(35) debits 37 and leaves 73 against duties of 75 (invoice 65, reserve 10), which is 2 short. Funding 112 would back one partial; each further partial charges another 2 that no duty reflects. That backing is a PROPOSED application policy. S13 allocate(true,23,7,2) needs at least 23 A and 4 B for non-negative custody; 25 A and 10 B is PROPOSED full backing, and S13 has no action discharging allocation_reserve.
assumptions: Source-only arithmetic, not execution. The V2 Close zero-duty condition is an uncompiled-source reading.
Even under the proposed 112 policy the reserve duty stays 10 and Close stays blocked; discharge or migration needs a program change.
S13 units is checked only arithmetically (23 = 3×7 + 2) and is never debited.

A program-asset fee is not debt repayment and not a network fee. Network fees, collateral, claim-output min-ADA and the V2 thread reserve (lovelace returned on Close) are separate funding items; a reserve duty is a program liability.
Delivery evidence and dispute rules remain named assumptions. Still needs independent open/partial/finish/reserve-return accounting and a backing-policy negative.

trustNotes.title: What the interactive page does
trustNotes.body: The invoice worksheet is local browser arithmetic over the S12 fixture values; it does not execute Moriarty, produce or check a proof, or create a transaction or ledger state. The explorer’s remove and restore control shows the consumer rule; a complete Web on this page is not proof verification, acceptance or settlement. Role cards state what each transition must prove; they do not claim fifteen independently implemented proof producers, and the supplied proof evidence concerns one invoice-partial relation. DEX, issuance and loan amounts are worked examples with no supplied source program; issuance additionally needs an application mint policy, which is distinct from the C2 claim policy. Identifiers shown in the explorer are placeholders. Cost: more Strands can duplicate context hashing, range constraints, exports, issuance and verification, and whole execution may be preferable; no measurement exists.

trustNotes.title: Permissionless use and retained scope
trustNotes.body: Moriarty is a permissionless language of provable intention: any developer may author, compile, prove, publish and deploy programs in the supported language without approval from Moriarty maintainers, an agent council, Foreman, a hosted solver or a program registry. Objective validity rules, resource costs and asset-owner authorization still apply, and application-specific access control remains expressible without becoming a deployment restriction. Optional hosted proving, relaying or indexing services are never required. groth16.title: How many Groth16 setups a Web needs
groth16.intro: Every Strand carries a Groth16 proof. Groth16 keys belong to one compiled relation, so the number of setups follows the number of distinct compiled circuits, not the number of transactions, users or claims.

concepts.label: Statement
concepts.title: Public inputs
concepts.body: The compiled relation fixes which values are public. Together they form the statement. They are not secret. A proof does not turn them into authenticated ledger facts: the validator rebuilds them from the transaction.

concepts.label: Witness
concepts.title: Private values
concepts.body: The witness is every other value that satisfies the constraints. The prover keeps it. The proof is zero-knowledge: it shows that the statement holds and reveals nothing else about the witness.

concepts.label: Proof and verification
concepts.title: Keys, proof, verifier
concepts.body: Setup for one relation outputs a proving key and a verification key. Both are public. The prover combines the proving key, the statement and the witness into a proof of three group elements. The verifier checks it against the verification key and the public inputs with one pairing-product equation.

groth16.setupIntro: Groth16 defines Setup as an algorithm over one relation. It does not prescribe a ceremony. A common practice splits the setup into two multi-party phases.

setupStages.label: Phase 1
setupStages.title: Shared powers of tau
setupStages.body: This phase produces reusable parameters for one curve, up to a maximum constraint capacity. Any circuit on that curve that fits the capacity and uses a compatible format can build on it.

setupStages.label: Phase 2
setupStages.title: One per compiled circuit
setupStages.body: Each exact compiled relation gets its own phase 2. The relation includes its constraints, its public-input layout and its bounds. The phase outputs that circuit's proving and verification keys.

counter.title: Setup stages for K compatible circuits
counter.body: Choose a number of distinct compiled circuits that share one curve and one phase-1 capacity. This is arithmetic, not a deployed inventory.
counter.label: Distinct compiled circuits (K)
counter.result: {K} circuits need one shared phase 1 and {K} circuit-specific phase 2 stages. That counts stages; it does not mean {K} + 1 complete ceremonies.
counter.conditions: This holds only if every circuit uses the same curve, fits the phase-1 capacity and accepts its format, and only if each phase has a verified transcript with at least one honest participant.

reuseExamples.title: Same relation, new values
reuseExamples.body: New transactions, users, assets and public-input values inside an unchanged compiled relation reuse its keys.

reuseExamples.title: Changed relation
reuseExamples.body: A new relation needs its own phase 2. A relation changes when its constraints, compiled program, bounds or public-input layout change, or when another Groth16 wrapper is added. Aggregating proofs does not remove the base circuits' setups.

reuseExamples.title: Bounded generic relations
reuseExamples.body: One parameterized relation with fixed bounds covers many claims without a new setup. It is not one unbounded circuit for all future Cardano applications.

groth16.trust: Proving and verification keys are public. The secret is the setup randomness, often called toxic waste. Anyone who holds it can produce verifying proofs for statements that have no witness, so it must not survive the setup. A multi-party phase is trustworthy when its transcript verifies and at least one participant in that phase was honest, under the protocol's assumptions. Every phase needs that property.
groth16.cardanoCount: The exact count is the number of distinct compiled circuits, including any wrappers, in a frozen circuit inventory. The 235 pre-dedup review identifiers, 20 families and seven layers describe review scope. None of them is a setup count. The circuit manifest is not frozen, so no total can be assigned yet.

sevenLayers.title: Seven layers of a Moriarty Web
sevenLayers.intro: Proving Nothing describes every zero-knowledge system through seven layers: interdependent concerns, not seven runtime phases that execute in order. Read through them, a Moriarty Web is one system: financial rules become constraints, a private witness satisfies them, Groth16 seals a proof for each Strand, and a Cardano consumer accepts the transition only when every required Strand matches the transaction it settles.

layers.name: Setup
layers.headline: Keys made for one compiled relation
layers.body: Groth16 derives proving and verifying keys from secret randomness for one compiled circuit. Each distinct compiled relation needs its own setup; the count follows circuits, not predicates or catalogue entries. Whoever keeps that randomness can forge proofs, so soundness assumes it is destroyed.
layers.mapping: Catalogue entries and owner intents name the verifying key.

layers.name: Language
layers.headline: Financial rules written as a program
layers.body: Moriarty programs state what an action may do: payment arithmetic, fees kept separate from repayment, caps an owner signs, and duties that continue. The compiler turns that source into constraints; a rule left unconstrained is a rule no proof enforces.
layers.mapping: Moriarty rules for payments, fees, caps and duties.

layers.name: Witness
layers.headline: Every step, recorded by the prover
layers.body: The prover runs the program over its inputs and records every intermediate value. Zero-knowledge keeps this assignment hidden, but only the assignment: amounts that appear in Cardano outputs or in the statement stay public. Witness generation must not leak values through its own behavior.
layers.mapping: One whole-execution witness can serve several Strand roles.

layers.name: Arithmetization
layers.headline: Every rule becomes an equation
layers.body: The compiled program becomes rank-1 constraints over a prime field, which Groth16 encodes as a quadratic arithmetic program. A valid witness satisfies every constraint. The public inputs carry a statement digest; an in-circuit BLAKE2b gadget ties them to the statement bytes.
layers.mapping: Caps, fees and duty updates become constraints.

layers.name: Proof System
layers.headline: A short certificate of correct computation
layers.body: Groth16 turns the witness into a constant-size proof checked by one pairing equation. Under an honest setup, knowledge soundness means a verifying proof shows the prover knew a satisfying witness; zero-knowledge means the proof reveals nothing beyond its statement. It never shows the statement's values describe the real ledger.

layers.name: Cryptographic Bedrock
layers.headline: Hard problems underneath
layers.body: A pairing-friendly elliptic curve supplies Groth16's groups and scalar field; Groth16's soundness argument holds in the generic bilinear group model. BLAKE2b collision resistance binds statement bytes to digests. Signatures authenticate owner intents and claimant releases. These primitives support the proof core and fix what it can express.
layers.mapping: Cardano scripts evaluate the pairing check and hashes.

layers.name: Verification
layers.headline: Proof meets ledger
layers.body: A claim policy checks each Groth16 proof and mints a proof-claim output. One settlement transaction consumes every Strand the Web requires; the validator rebuilds each statement from the transaction and spent state, requires claimant signatures and enforces signed caps. Outside facts need a named issuer, authentication path and freshness limit.

sevenLayers.relationshipsTitle: How the layers lean on each other
relationships: Layers 4, 5 and 6 form the proof core: the scalar field, the R1CS encoding and Groth16's pairing check are chosen as one design, not three.
Setup follows the compiled relation. Changing a rule changes the circuit, and a changed circuit needs a new setup and a new verifying key.
The proof and the ledger divide the work. Layers 3 to 5 show the statement's arithmetic is correct; Layer 7 checks, from the transaction itself, that the statement describes this step.
The verifier reaches down. Cardano scripts must run the pairing check, which constrains the curve and proof system beneath them.
The numbering follows how a reader meets the system, not the order of engineering decisions; the dependency lists here sketch the main pressures, not a complete graph.
